purpose: Cabozantinib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including kidney cancer, liver cancer, and a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid cancer. It may also be used for other cancers as determined by your doctor. It is often used when other treatments have not worked or are not suitable.
how_it_works: Cancer cells need certain proteins called kinases to grow and spread. Cabozantinib works by blocking several of these proteins, essentially cutting off the signals that tell cancer cells to grow and multiply. It also helps stop tumors from forming new blood vessels, which they need to survive and spread.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, decreased appetite, tiredness, mouth sores, high blood pressure, weight loss, constipation, swelling or pain in the hands and feet (hand-foot syndrome), and changes in hair color. Some patients also experience stomach pain or changes in taste.
warnings: This medication can cause serious bleeding, holes or tears in the stomach or intestines, and problems with wound healing — so tell your doctor before any surgery. It can raise your blood pressure significantly, so your blood pressure will need to be monitored. Rare but serious side effects include blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and liver problems. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice as it can affect how the drug works. Do not take if pregnant, and use effective birth control during treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with cabozantinib.
typical_dosing: The usual dose depends on which cancer is being treated and which brand you are prescribed. For Cabometyx, the typical dose is 60 mg taken by mouth once daily, but it may be reduced to 40 mg or 20 mg if side effects occur. For Cometriq, capsules are taken as two separate doses per day. Always take it on an empty stomach — do not eat for at least 1 hour before and at least 2 hours after taking it. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole; do not crush or chew it.
